ops.title: A lane's idle_notification with idleReason \"failed\" (network/API error) is not proof of death — probe before re-dispatching a replacement
ops.body:
A background lane that emits `idleReason: "failed"` with a transient cause (ENOTFOUND, API stream error, rate limit) can resume on its own when the fault clears — it is parked, not dead. Re-dispatching a replacement onto the same worktree creates two live agents racing one shared working copy (hit twice in the cc-transcript v14 rewrite: p6-sweep vs p6-sweep-2, resolved only because both agents detected the sibling and refused to clobber).

**Why:** the idle notification reports the *turn's* failure, not the agent's lifecycle. Usage-limit deaths ("session limit reached") genuinely end the lane; transient network faults usually don't.

**How to apply:** before re-dispatching a "dead" lane, (1) SendMessage the original and give it one wake cycle to respond, and/or (2) watch its worktree for fresh commits/mtime churn. Only spawn a successor (adoption protocol) when the probe stays silent AND the failure reason is a hard one (usage/session limit). If a successor is spawned anyway, its brief must name the risk and require a sibling check before first edit. Related: [[named-agents-need-report-nudge]].
